infrastructure: Slovakia has reasonable broadband connectivity in urban areas, with EU-funded rural expansion programmes.
Bratislava has basic data centre infrastructure, benefiting from proximity to Vienna and Budapest.
5G deployment is in early stages, with major operators beginning rollout in 2023–2024.
talent: Slovak Technical University and Comenius University have computer science programmes with AI research.
Brain drain to Austria, Germany, and the Czech Republic is severe due to wage differentials.
A small population (5.5M) fundamentally limits the absolute talent pool.
governance: Slovakia has a functioning democratic system with GDPR compliance, though governance quality has been variable.
Recent political changes have created some governance uncertainty.
The Office for Personal Data Protection provides GDPR enforcement.
investment: Slovakia has attracted automotive FDI (Volkswagen, Kia, Stellantis), creating industrial AI adjacency.
EU structural funds are the primary digital transformation investment driver.
Domestic AI startup investment is very limited.
economic_readiness: One of Europe's highest automotive manufacturing intensities per capita creates AI automation demand.
Strong industrial base but limited services sector AI adoption.
Lower GDP per capita and small market size limit domestic AI product opportunities.
